back: Tokens are conditionally independent given the class, so $P(x\mid c)=\prod_i\theta_{c,w_i}$.
An unseen word would give $\theta=0$ and zero out the class; pseudo-counts keep every probability positive. It equals a symmetric Dirichlet prior.
Products of many probabilities underflow; logs turn them into sums without changing the arg max.
log_prior $(C,)$, log_theta $(C,V)$; scores for a count matrix: X @ log_theta.T + log_prior, shape $(N,C)$.

front: Naive Bayes vs logistic regression on text
back: NB: counting, fast, good with little data, over-confident probabilities. LR: gradient training, one weight per feature, better with more data and correlated features.
Macro averages per-class F1 (rare classes count equally); micro pools counts (frequent classes dominate).

front: Why is accuracy misleading on imbalanced text data?
back: Predicting the majority class already scores high; check minority-class precision and recall.
Per-class metrics, threshold or prior shift, class weights, resampling (train split only), more minority data.
Use bigrams, or prefix NOT_ to tokens after a negator until the next punctuation.
Reading validation mistakes, grouping them by cause (negation, sarcasm, domain shift, label noise) and fixing the largest group first.

front: Why are NB probabilities poorly calibrated?
back: Treating correlated words as independent counts the same evidence repeatedly, pushing probabilities towards 0 and 1.
